source_text: Iustificati ergo ex fide pacem habemus ad Deum per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum. Gloriamur in spe gloriae Dei; tribulatio patientiam operatur.
orientation: Origen is quoting and briefly glossing Paul's words from Romans 5 about the results of justification by faith.
pass_a_gloss: Justified therefore out of faith peace we have toward God through Lord our Jesus Christ. We glory in hope of glory of God; tribulation patience works.

choices.english: Therefore, having been justified out of faith
choices.why: Keeps the passive participle force of Iustificati and the source preposition ex to show faith as the source or basis of justification, matching the glossary's 'faith' rendering.
The preposition ad with Deum indicates direction or relation, so 'toward God' preserves the spatial metaphor of the Latin rather than flattening it to 'with God'.

choices.english: We glory in the hope of the glory of God
choices.why: The verb gloriamur is middle/passive in form but active in sense; 'we glory' keeps the same root as gloria, and 'in the hope' preserves the preposition in.
rejected: We boast in hope of God's glory
We exult in the hope of the glory of God

choices.why: Operatur is deponent with active meaning; 'works' keeps the productive, causal force of the verb, and 'patience' is the standard rendering of patientia.

bible_refs.note: Iustificati ergo ex fide pacem habemus ad Deum per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum. Gloriamur in spe gloriae Dei; tribulatio patientiam operatur.

pass_b_english: Therefore, having been justified out of faith, we have peace toward God through our Lord Jesus Christ. We glory in the hope of the glory of God; tribulation works patience (Romans 5:1-3).
